summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from RIT with robotics and embedded systems experience across sensor integration, hardware interfacing in C/C++, and computer vision. Built a voice-controlled robotic pick-and-place system with TensorRT YOLO visual servoing, two-link IK in C++, and contact-fused grasping — resolving 11 hardware integration failures to reach 100% pick reliability.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi Pico and HC-05 Bluetooth to translate 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands via Python.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Led a 25-member robotics team across national competitions, owning mechanical design, PCB fabrication, and AI/ML software integration end-to-end.
Designed and fabricated custom PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.

experience.title: Research Intern
bullets: Deployed ZoeDepth monocular depth estimation for crack-depth profiling with ±8% error; architected full metal inspection pipeline using image stitching, wavelet denoising, and depth estimation (PSNR 86).

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Achieved 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials) at ~11.5s end-to-end latency; resolved 11 hardware integration failures including servo crosstalk, false-positive detections, and rolling-shutter depth errors.
Built a three-layer pipeline (Flutter → Flask-SocketIO → Jetson+Arduino) with TensorRT YOLO at ~18 FPS, dual VL53L0X ToF sensors via I2C mux, and two-link IK in C++ driving five servos.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used YOLOv8 on NVIDIA Jetson to detect and track objects; sent real-time motor control commands to STM32 over UART with interrupt-driven multi-servo PWM control.
Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination; integrated VL53L0X ToF sensor for distance-based targeting.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Programmed Cortex-M4 peripherals in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1); achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at deterministic 1 Hz update rate.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C driver; verified in Proteus.

awards: Ranked 10th, Robocon — National-level robotics competition among 45 universities (2022)
1st Prize, Poster Presentation — 2D and 3D Image Mosaicing of Microscopic Images, F.C.R.I.T. (2024)
